newsitem.title: USA: Triarc sets beverage unit spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Triarc sets beverage unit spin-off.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc said Monday directors approved a plan to offer up to 20 percent of the shares of its beverage and restaurant businesses to the public and spin off the remainder of the shares to Triarc holders.

The initial public offering and spinoff will be subject to, among other things, receipt of a favorable ruling from the Internal Revenue Service that the spinoff will be tax-free to the company and its stockholders, Triarc said.
The request for the ruling from the IRS will contain several complex issues, it noted. The offering and spinoff are not expected before the end of 1997's second quarter.
Triarc further announced the establishment of the Triarc Beverage Group, which will oversee the operations of Triarc's two beverage subsidiaries, Royal Crown Co Inc and Mistic Brands Inc.

Michael F. Weinstein, chief executive officer of Mistic, will become the chief executive officer of the Triarc Beverage Group. John Carson, president of Royal Crown, will become chairman of the group. Triarc Beverage will be headquartered in White Plains, N.Y.

After the spinoff, Triarc Cos will consist of National Propane Corp, in its capacity as the managing general partner, with an about 44 percent interest in National Propane Partners LP and C.H. Patrick, a maker of dyes and specialty chemicals.
Triarc said it will also have about $200 million in cash that will be available for future acquisitions and investments.
It said the new consumer products company will be comprised of the Triarc Restaurant Group -- Arby's Inc, p.t. Noodle's, T.J. Cinnamons and ZuZu -- and the beverage group.

Commenting on the planned spinoff, Triarc explained, "We would like to expand our restaurant and beverage businesses by developing our existing brands and acquiring and developing additional product lines. We believe that the ability to raise the capital needed to fund this expansion will be significantly enhanced by having our beverage and restaurant businesses separate from Triarc.

"In addition, it will also be possible for the beverage and restaurant company to allow its key constituencies to directly participate in its growth of these businesses through equity ownership in them."
The company also noted the "offering will provide us with some of the growth capital we will need to fulfill our vision." -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
